Quarterly roll-forward Upside & EV Upside now use Q4 2027 Posted 30 Sep 2026, 10:51 pm EDT

As Q3 ends and Q4 begins on October 1, we have rolled the reference quarter for Upside and EV Upside from Q3 2027 to Q4 2027. This keeps the dashboard focused roughly 12 months ahead. The change was applied on September 30, just ahead of the new quarter.

  • Upside: Q4 2027 target price divided by the current share price.
  • EV Upside: Uses the same Q4 2027 target and current share price, with the existing Base-score weighting.

Figures can change because we are looking one quarter further ahead, not necessarily because a company’s outlook has been upgraded. The roll-forward itself does not change Base scores or quarterly forecasts.

Next planned roll-forward: January 1, 2027.

Model update September 28–30: Q3 2027 model-ceiling changes Posted 30 Sep 2026, 11:45 am EDT

Scroll within this bulletin for all 10 updates. Percentages are changes to model ceilings, not share-price returns.

  • LITE +15.15%: Added a 30% probability-weighted scenario for substantially higher optical circuit switching revenue.
  • MediaTek (2454.TW) +9.34%: Incorporated a 30% probability-weighted uplift from higher custom AI chip revenue forecasts.
  • NRGV +5.96%: Added probability-weighted earnings from acquired Goshe power projects, allowing for associated costs.
  • NBIS +5.75%: Incorporated October’s 20% GPU pricing increase and two assumed 15% increases in 2027.
  • Sivers (SIVE.ST) +2.36%: Raised customer-conversion probabilities as emerging optical architectures strengthen demand for its lasers.
  • LPKF (LPK.DE) +2.13%: Higher probability-weighted glass-substrate tool capture outweighed the modeled production delay.
  • AAOI +1.29%: Added probability-weighted higher 800G/1.6T utilization while retaining existing capacity and pricing assumptions.
  • Broadcom (AVGO) +1.09%: Incorporated a 25% probability-weighted uplift from higher AI semiconductor revenue forecasts.
  • AMD −0.96%: Added estimated acquisition-related share dilution without increasing operating forecasts.
  • Micron (MU) 0%: Stronger supply-agreement coverage raised the artifact Base from 88 to 90, while its ceiling and Excel Base of 99 stayed unchanged.
